reviewer: Codex, independent; did not author v1 or v2
protocol: Independent adversarial review; refute not confirm; other current v2 reviewer not read
reviewScope: Review only. This review does not mark DR-112 SATISFIED, does not qualify or demonstrate anything, does not authorize implementation, and does not apply or seal the candidate.
summary: The source pins and verbatim carries reproduce, the candidate preserves separate roles and no-network behavior, the P-8/SC-OPS provenance repair is honest, and it mints no quorum, clock, emergency, or waiver values. The central repairs do not hold, however. The transition relation remains partial for named pairs whose guards do not match, contradicts its precedence rule on later clock observations, omits the claimed recovery abort, and does not actually accept revoke/quorum observations from every non-UNBOOTSTRAPPED state. TRUSTED entry treats an inactive envelope/preimage check as if the complete trust predicate held and root recovery still lacks an authority relation for accepting a new root. The purported total continuation table gives both drain and refuse language for the same CORE-expired/stale tuple. Refusal audit exists, but its reason remains optional. At 3 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, DR-112 remains OPEN and this verdict authorizes no implementation.

blockers.title: The machine is still not a total deterministic event relation, and the claimed recovery abort does not exist
blockers.measurement: The 7 states and 8 events yield 56 state/event pairs. Thirty-six pairs are named by at least one transition member and 20 fall under defaultTransition. But the default applies only when a pair is not named; it supplies no outcome when a named pair has no true guard. Concrete examples are ST-TRUSTED/EV-CLOCK while the snapshot is neither expired nor stale, and ST-TRUSTED/EV-QUORUM-OBSERVE when the observed signer count is not below threshold. Those ordinary observations match a named pair but no transition and no else outcome. The same gap exists for guard-false install/revocation cases unless an unrelated local sentence happens to supply an else.
blockers.precedenceConflict: From ST-STALE-REVOCATION, a later EV-CLOCK that observes metadataExpiry has no named transition, so defaultTransition says stay ST-STALE-REVOCATION and REFUSE. statePrecedence simultaneously says ST-EXPIRED must be the visible state because EXPIRED dominates STALE-REVOCATION. From ST-RECOVERY, an expiry observation similarly yields stay RECOVERY by the default while precedence says EXPIRED dominates RECOVERY. The artifact does not state which rule wins, so the global precedence sentence does not make the transition relation deterministic.
blockers.claimedCoverageMismatch: honestyRepairsFromV1 says EV-REVOKE and EV-QUORUM-OBSERVE operate from every non-UNBOOTSTRAPPED state. Mechanically, EV-REVOKE omits ST-REVOKED; EV-QUORUM-OBSERVE omits ST-QUORUM-LOST and ST-REVOKED. A newer revocation presented while already revoked therefore defaults to REFUSE instead of accepting and advancing the monotonic observation. This is not merely a wording mismatch: it defeats the declared rule that revocation observations are monotonic state.
blockers.recoveryAbort: No event or transition exits ST-RECOVERY on an operator abort or failed ceremony. EV-RECOVER-BEGIN guard failure occurs before entry and is not an abort. In ST-RECOVERY, invalid EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD and invalid EV-RECOVER-COMMIT both stay RECOVERY; EV-RECOVER-BEGIN itself is a default stay-and-refuse. The only exits are a successful commit, a revocation observation, or a below-threshold quorum observation. fixtureClasses/6 nevertheless claims an abort/refusal case, and the recovery-payload ordering is also unresolved: presentation from a pre-recovery state defaults to refusal, while BEGIN requires ceremony inputs already present.
blockers.whyBlocker: DR-112's acceptance cell expressly requires a reviewed state machine, and SITCV1-B1 required total deterministic behavior plus a recovery abort. A relation with unmatched named guards, conflicting global/default targets, and no abort cannot serve as that safety machine or deterministically populate the required audit record.
blockers.minimumRepair: Make the fallback apply whenever no guarded transition matches, and define whether ordinary no-change observations are accepted or refused. Encode precedence in the transition function for every relevant source state. Either accept and monotonically record revoke/quorum observations from every claimed non-UNBOOTSTRAPPED state or narrow the claim with a safety justification. Add an explicit audited recovery-abort event and target, define recovery-payload ordering, and exercise fresh-clock, restored-quorum, repeated-revocation, precedence, and actual abort cases. Preserve all numeric reservations and deferrals.

blockers.title: TRUSTED entry remains fail-open and root recovery has no authorizing relation
blockers.measurement: Every transition to ST-TRUSTED says all requiredOnEveryTrustedEntry items hold, but the envelopePreimageJoin item expressly says its verification is INACTIVE until ID-DEP-1 and the ceremony close, and the bootstrap guard repeats that exception. The active DR-103 checks are only UNSIGNED and DIGEST_MISMATCH: they establish envelope presence and byte/digest custody, not a valid cryptographic envelope. Consequently the written transition can enter ST-TRUSTED while a required trust check is inactive. trustPolicyShape.failedGuard does not make dependency-inactive a refusal, and FC-TRUST-POLICY unconditionally demands wrong-key/threshold refusals while leaving envelope mismatch inactive.
blockers.recoveryAuthorityGap: The recovery commit applies bootstrapAnchorCustody to 'new roots'. That predicate says the presented root is the already accepted install-scoped anchor. A genuinely new root cannot satisfy that literal predicate, while accepting it as self-supplied would violate the same predicate. No rule states which old root, recovery key set, or separately named authority may authorize rotation/recovery. roleToKeyAndDelegatedNamespace authorizes release signers for a role/namespace; it is not a transition relation from an accepted old root to an authorized replacement. Thus commit is either impossible or circular/fail-open, the same recovery-authority omission measured in SITCV1-B2.
blockers.whyBlocker: The accepted DR-103 split deliberately leaves envelope/key/delegation/threshold ceremony validity to DR-112. A state named TRUSTED cannot be reached by treating an inactive cryptographic check as satisfied, and the row's required recovery ceremony cannot accept a replacement root without a non-self-authorizing chain.
blockers.minimumRepair: Make dependency-inactive envelope verification fail closed for TRUSTED entry, or explicitly condition the entire executable transition/fixture surface on activation of both ID-DEP-1 and DR-112 envelope semantics; do not invent canonicalization. Define a parameterized, non-numeric old-root/recovery-authority-to-new-root authorization relation for rotation and recovery, and require it on commit. Add hostile forged-envelope and unauthorized-replacement-root fixtures while keeping threshold, clock, and participant values reserved.

blockers.title: The continuation table still gives no single decision for a CORE-expired or CORE-stale system
blockers.measurement: For the concrete tuple CORE=ST-EXPIRED, INDEX=ST-TRUSTED, COMPONENT=ST-TRUSTED (and likewise CORE=ST-STALE-REVOCATION), totalDecision[1].alreadyRunning says both that an existing process 'may drain' if later roles allow it and 'preview: refuse'. 'Drain' and 'new privileged work' are not outcomes in the declared already-running-versus-new-process model, and no rule defines either term. The CORE-first/first-fail-closed precedence cannot resolve the row: if the CORE row is a refusal it ends evaluation; if it permits drain, the later all-TRUSTED row does not match because CORE is not TRUSTED. The same event therefore has a permissive and a refusing reading.
blockers.fixtureGap: FC-CONTINUE-PRECEDENCE calls three selected tuples a 'Cross-product' but does not cover the ambiguous CORE-expired/stale tuple or the state cross-product. It therefore cannot force one interpretation of the row.
blockers.whyBlocker: Emergency/current-component continuation is part of the live DR-112 row and SITCV1-B3 required a total conflict-resolved decision table. An undefined limited-drain category plus a contradictory refusal is not a deterministic offline-running policy.
blockers.minimumRepair: Choose one typed alreadyRunning outcome for CORE expiry/staleness. If bounded drain is intended, define it as a distinct decision with enforceable limits and state how it composes with INDEX and COMPONENT; otherwise remove the permissive text and state REFUSE. Expand the fixture requirement to the role-state cross-product or an equivalent exhaustive generated table, including CORE expired and stale cases.

shouldFix.title: A refused event may still be audited without a refusal reason
shouldFix.detail: The audit shape declares refusalReason? optional, including when outcome=refused. FC-REFUSAL-AUDIT asserts only outcome=refused and to==from. The permitted v1 verdict's required repair called for a typed outcome/refusal reason, and guard failures can have materially different causes even for the same state/event pair. A reasonless record proves that something refused but not which safety guard did so.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Require a stable typed refusalReason exactly when outcome=refused, forbid it or define its standing when accepted, and require negative fixtures to assert the expected reason. Keep this operational metadata, not sealed evidence.
